chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Wrestling in Kansas and why he never boxed
summary: Dance asks about wrestling, and Clayton explains how he did a preliminary bout as a teenager and avoided boxing to protect his lip.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Ah, I just want to interrupt. When you were out there before, what about the
Oh I did that in Kansas.
Well you skipped that though. You better put that in. How come you got into that?
Oh well, I'll tell you. I had a friend, a Greek fellow, his name was Hallas. and he was such a beautiful wrestler.

HALLAS. Billy Hallas. And he was a genius, a very good wrestler and a nice person. So everybody around my town was trying to be wrestlers at that time because we all went to his matches. So one day two promoters came down to my school and was asking people, young kids if they would like to be on the preliminaries to one of these big bouts that Billy was going to wrestle. And I told them yes I would like to be on it and make fifteen dollars.

And another boy named Herman Higginbotham, he was about fifty pounds heavier than I was. So we went on and we wrestled on the preliminaries and made fifteen dollars a piece. But that's as far as it went.
I never did want to be a wrestler.
Did you have any knowledge of how to do it, I mean? How to wrestle?
Yes. I mean there's a lot of tricks to that.
Yes. Well we studied that in that in school, yes. We used to know all the holds and locks. Yes, we knew that. We could wrestle. I could wrestle pretty good.
Well did you do some of this when you went out to California?

No, I never did wrestle. I could have boxed if I wanted to. And I didn't want to box because I wanted to play trumpet and you know, you get hit in the mouth boxing, even if you win, you might get hit in the mouth and then you can't play trumpet. So, I did everything. I washed dishes in Los Angeles. As I said, I worked in a pool hall. come
